title: a task's stack is freed while on-stack envs still point into it, and the GC then marks freed memory
live_proof: upstream fixed it in cb51fce92 (cb51fce921fc7beceb5337231c0e17b7299c1279) (2026-07-31), which is in master and postdates the 4.0.0-rc2 pin (2026-03-12); the pin's tree has no such fix. Host ASan at the pin: SIGABRT (with MRB_HEAP_PAGE_SIZE=1: SIGABRT); the same case on master: no report; capi.c at the pin, host ASan: heap-use-after-free in gc_mark_children on the freed task stack; with cb51fce92's task.c hunks: no report (probe/native-control.sh NC_ASAN=1, 2026-10-11)
fidelity: a C-API reduction of the Ruby test upstream added with its fix. At the 4.0.0-rc2 pin no Ruby script reaches the defect (trigger.rb, upstream's test extracted onto a harness, is kept as the record of what upstream ran): Task#close arrived upstream in 306d265cd (2026-07-14), after the pin, and mrb_execute_proc_synchronously and mrb_task_init_context are C API that upstream's test reaches only through C helpers (TaskTest) in mrbtest. capi.c does what upstream's TaskTest.run_sync test does, without the helper: it runs a proc whose closure escapes into $esc through mrb_execute_proc_synchronously, which frees the temporary task's stack without detaching the env, prints CASE11 ready, and runs a full collection, which marks the env and reads e->stack[i] on the freed stack. probe/build-capi.sh links it against each arm's own libmruby.a; probe/native-control.sh builds it natively against the pin and against the pin with cb51fce92's task.c hunks alone. What the driver does NOT establish is which arm ought to catch it
fault_sites_why: the GC's marking path from mrb_full_gc down to the read of e->stack[i] in gc_mark_children's MRB_TT_ENV case, which the inliner may fold into any caller on it. Upstream's fix message (cb51fce92) reports the crash at mrb_gc_mark under gc_mark_children (MRB_TT_ENV, e->stack[i]) under mrb_full_gc; capi.c built natively against the pin (probe/native-control.sh) crashes with SIGSEGV in mrb_gc_mark under gc_mark_children, incremental_marking_phase, incremental_gc, incremental_gc_finish, mrb_full_gc (gdb, 2026-10-11)., and its AddressSanitizer build (NC_ASAN=1) reports heap-use-after-free, READ of size 4, in gc_mark_children (gc.c:837) on a 1024-byte block freed by mrb_free in mrb_execute_proc_synchronously (task.c:1199) and allocated in task_init_context: the task's stack. With the fix's hunks neither build reports anything. The list was written after two staged runs of capi.c on each virtual image had already faulted in gc_mark_children; it is upstream's and the native run's path, not theirs.

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: abort: the C runtime stops it (not a capability fault)

status: sysalloc-none and sysalloc-bounds measured 2026-10-06 on the Capstone application VM and cheribsd-revocation on 2026-10-06 on CheriBSD purecap, all three with trigger.rb, which does not reach the defect at the pin; virtual-malloc and virtual-nested-pools measured 2026-10-11 on the virtual profile with capi.c; sysalloc-bounds (results/2026-10-11-system-group/bounds, not a verdict field: the bounds-only baseline) and cheribsd-revocation re-measured 2026-10-11 with capi.c.
